name: Isomorphic Prime Factorization Constraint
description: Replaced the original $x^3+y^3=9$ constraint with $(x+3)^y + (y+3)^x = 21$. Both map $\{1,2\}\times\{1,2\}$ to a set of values where only the heterogeneous pair $(1,2)$ yields a value whose prime factors divide the target product, strictly enforcing bipartiteness without the recognizable $x^3+y^3$ fingerprint.
